deviations: Web search: only two searches ran before the session-wide web-search budget was exhausted, so no press reports could be searched for tallies. This is the main reason coalition_only and final_vote_record are blank for seqs 54, 57, 61, 64, 67, 70, 73, 79 and for the third reading of seq 85.

The Knesset's own sites (main.knesset.gov.il, fs.knesset.gov.il) redirect to a geo-block page. Gazette PDFs, protocols and bill files were read only through Internet Archive captures, using the 'id_' (raw) form of the given capture URLs.

Sources beyond those the sheet names explicitly: Open Knesset mirrors of the Knesset's plenum-session tables (kns_plenumsession, kns_plmsessionitem, kns_documentplenumsession), bill tables (kns_bill, kns_documentbill) and kns_status. I treated these as Knesset records for reading dates and agenda items.
First-reading dates for seqs 54, 57, 61, 67, 70, 73 and 79 come from plenum agenda items with status 111 ('for plenum debate ahead of first reading'), not from a recorded first-reading vote.

Coalition composition comes from the Knesset member-position table (kns_persontoposition): the factions of ministers and deputy ministers in office on the vote date. It does not capture factions that supported the government without holding posts.

Internet Archive: of the protocols needed, only 17_ptm_129704.doc (19.7.2006, seq 82) and 15_ptm_532783.docx (31.7.2000, first reading of seq 64) had captures. Protocols for the final votes of seqs 54–79 and 85 had none.

Old Knesset record pages (knesset.gov.il/tql/knesset_new/...) for 1.2.2000 and 27.11.2000 exist only as bot-challenge captures with no content. Their use as Knesset record captures outside the fs.knesset.gov.il/<knesset>/Plenum/ path is noted.
The archive refused connections intermittently, and some fetch attempts failed for that reason.
NYU mirror (archive.nyu.edu): its Knesset holdings appear to be a settlement-themed selection, and title searches found no session on any passage date.
Explanatory notes were reached only for seq 57 (archived bill PDF 14_ls1_291112.PDF). Other bill files had no captures.

Hebrew Wikisource (Basic Law: The Knesset; Basic Law: The President) was consulted for current section texts as context for seqs 70 and 73. I also fetched the gazette PDF 16_lsr_299861.pdf (the 2003 'Amendment No. 6') to establish what else passed on 28.7.2003.

Possible frame defects: the page for seq 79 (ס"ח 1898, p. 524) also carries a second Basic Law passed the same day, the 2003 'Basic Law: The President of the State (Amendment No. 6)', plus the State Comptroller Law (Amendment No. 34). For seq 73 the other Basic Law is Basic Law: The Knesset (Amendment No. 34), per the Knesset bill table. For seq 57, the gazette date (25.3.1998) and the Knesset session table (24.3.1998) differ.
No court judgment or litigation page was opened. One web-search result list included press pages on the 2018 Jerusalem amendment; none was opened or used.
Gazette texts were taken from the PDFs' text layers. A few OCR misreadings were corrected in quotations (for example ר' for ד' in the seq 54 footnote; section numbers misread as 5ג/גג for 33).

No files were written, per the caller's instruction (the sheet's scratch-subfolder step was therefore not followed). All downloads were processed in memory; the tool harness itself saved two large outputs to its own tool-results folder.
